speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the implementation status of the Police's PolCam 2.0 project across Singapore; (b) what specific abnormalities can the system detect; (c) what information and analytics does the system collect on a routine and on-demand or ad hoc basis; (d) what privacy concerns does the Ministry have with regard to the system; and (e) how have these concerns been mitigated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The system will then alert the Police operators, and Police resources can be dispatched, if necessary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Polcams, including the versions before PolCam 2.0, in general, have proven to be very useful in helping the Police deter and solve crimes, including unlicensed moneylending, theft and outrage of modesty.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The deployment of cameras is crucial in deterring and dealing with crime and any terrorist activity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police will continue to install more cameras.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our approach has broad support from the public and has resulted in people feeling safe.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Public confidence and trust in the Police Force remains high.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Among the survey respondents who felt safer than before, the installation of Polcams in the estates was one of the top factors contributing to their perception that the neighbourhood is safer.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF has data protection safeguards and controls on the use of Polcam footage.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The footage is securely stored, and only authorised persons are allowed to access them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Any officer found accessing the footage for unauthorised purposes will be severely dealt with.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I just have three supplementary questions for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The third question is how soon is data wiped out under PolCam 2.0, compared to PolCam 1.0?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On how soon the data is wiped out, I am not able to reveal that because of operational considerations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As for the audit and the regularity of audit and the other question on whether the regime is more restricted, we already have a very strict regime.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The whole point is to ensure that we maintain public trust and confidence, and audit is something that we do very regularly.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have strict protocols and we ensure that, as I have mentioned, access is restricted and tightly controlled.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Any persons found using the footages or accessing the information for unauthorised purposes will be severely dealt with.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that there are 5,000 cameras already implemented.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This is a final supplementary question for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: How often are audits conducted to ensure that the information is secure?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I think it is sufficient to say that audits are conducted on a regular basis.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I am not at liberty to discuss exactly how the Police conduct their internal operations, but it would suffice to say that audits are done on a very regular basis.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Checks are also conducted as and when there is a need, for example, when there are irregularities.
